message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | 1. **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
2. **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
3. **Draw Two (+2)** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
4. **Wild** – Player chooses the new color.
5. **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – Player chooses the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise you can be challenged.) | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your **second‑to‑last** card, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Draw Two, Skip, Reverse = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. First to reach the agreed‑upon point total wins the game. | | **House Rules (optional)** | • “Draw Two” and “Wild Draw Four” can be stacked.
• “Wild Draw Four” can be challenged if the player could have played a different card.
• “Skip” can be played on a “Skip” to skip two players.
• “Reverse” on a two‑player game acts like a “Skip.” | **Quick Tips** - Keep an eye on the color you’re running out of; try to play it early. - Use “Wild” cards strategically to change the color to one you have many of. - Remember to shout “UNO!”—it’s a simple but crucial rule! Enjoy your game!
